## Purpose

## ADDED Requirements

### Requirement: Verified effect admission

A governed profile MUST deny protected actions when policy or required identity/context is unavailable, and expose the denial posture.

| Dependency | Existing scope / location | Required convergence checkpoint |

Record current owner and the agreed API/approval/history contract. Do not infer completion from an old waypoint. Overlapping implementation waits for owner agreement or merged release checkpoint. |
| D-MINI | Original mini local shipping commits diverge from origin/main; original full pack has uncommitted distribution/context changes | Reconcile exact shipped/accepted commit through the owning work. Never replace it with an older pin because the branch name matches. Reuse merged agent-team skills. |
| D-FRF | Fabric `codex/production-readiness-integration`, with pending work and local commits | Map agent-control semantics, identity, shape/replay/sync and observer features to accepted work before new implementation. |
| D-FORGE | Forge production-readiness branch plus database-role and GraphQL worktrees | Agree domain-write/outbox/RLS/shape contract; preserve role and GraphQL changes. |

| D-KNOWME | App `main`; system `feat/embedded-memory-crud` with vendor/config/spec WIP | Preserve app/system identities, Rust-core ownership, consent and embedding contracts; explicitly reconcile any duplicate local loop. |
| D-MEMORY | surreal-memory original dependency branch and newer fetched main | Record exact auth/namespace/storage API and pins. Sharing uses a service or designated in-process handle, never two processes opening one embedded directory. |

No messages or dispatches were sent to the other task. Ownership described here is a planning reservation based on its recorded plan, not an agreement to transfer work.

## Merge protocol

1. Before a slice starts, fetch only; record default-branch and dependency SHAs and compare with the manifest. Do not auto-pull or rebase an active writer's branch.
2. Classify each relevant incoming change as already merged, dependency to adopt, conflicting contract, or unrelated. Review exact commits and uncommitted work boundaries with the owner.
3. Incorporate an agreed immutable checkpoint into this initiative's corresponding worktree. No force-push, reset, broad stash or cherry-pick of guessed fixes. Update the manifest and compatibility matrix in the same planned change.
4. Implement one coherent slice and validate its real boundary. Merge provider capability before dependent consumers require it; use capability negotiation or a documented compatibility window.
5. Commit submodule/git dependency pins only after the target commit is available from its configured remote. A collection of matching branches is never an atomic release.

The convergence branches are local planning branches. No new PR, remote publication or deployment is implied by their creation. Future PRs should be small ordered slices; avoid one long-running ecosystem-wide merge.

## Resource isolation

Use separate Rust target directories, Node outputs, test workspaces, database files/namespaces, app-data directories, queues, ports and service credentials for convergence. Do not modify installed skill deployment, launch agents, shared Docker volumes or the running UAR/Boss services to test this branch. Reserve one local Rust build writer at a time while the existing integration uses this memory-constrained host. Plan platform runners before expensive compilation.

Only this directory's independent KBD identity is activated. Product roots may contain tracked identities or absolute `focus_project_path` fields copied from another checkout: do not run their KBD commands until ownership/identity isolation is explicitly resolved. Use the initiative's exact path for every transition. Local logs and memory indexes are evidence, not shared write locks.

## Initial ownership

The convergence planner owns this planning directory and the 11 new branch/worktree registrations. No product implementation file is claimed yet. A future dispatch must name repository, change/task IDs, file/module write scope, dependency checkpoint, model/harness, output directory and review owner. Two sessions may read the same source; only one writes a given assigned surface.

## Recovery rules across modes

- Viewer disconnect, process death, device suspension and host loss are different events with different contracts. Detached work survives viewer loss only; process survival needs a resident owner or explicit recovery.
- Event replay, snapshot restoration, native-session resume and workflow continuation are separate advertised capabilities. Retention gaps are visible and require resnapshot/reconciliation.
- Every retry distinguishes transport delivery from model generation, agent attempt and external side effect. Unknown outcomes are reconciled; cancellation cannot erase prior effects.
- Subscribe, deliver content, expand a payload and act are separate authorization checks. Queueing cannot preserve a revoked grant indefinitely.
- A declined or unreachable explicitly selected external instance is not permission to spawn the bundled one.
- Mobile local grants have a declared validity window. Sensitive remote effects require fresh authority; offline edits remain pending when that authority is unavailable.
- No universal exactly-once promise: a target without idempotency or reliable result lookup uses an explicit uncertain-outcome/manual-reconciliation path.

# Analysis: agent-fabric-convergence

This stage reuses the five completed research packages and proposed standard, then reconciles their design choices with the fetched source evidence. No new framework or dependency is selected from memory. External library versions and mutable protocol documentation must be refreshed through Context7/primary sources when a concrete implementation adopts them. This is reuse analysis, not a repeat landscape survey or a claim of fresh upstream validation.

## Decisions

1. **Use the existing UAR host.** Extend its thread, actor, compiler and policy boundaries for teams. A second token/tool loop would conflict with existing attenuation and mobile embedding. A team coordinator schedules distinct bounded runs; BossFang may own a larger application workflow containing those runs.
2. **Adopt the current P1 integration as a dependency.** The new UAR driver and BossFang HTTP provider bridge supersede earlier missing-foundation findings. Agree checkpoint, history vocabulary and file ownership before changing their shared interfaces. The initiative must not absorb or delay the other task's current delivery.
3. **Separate logical identities.** Definitions, installations, activations, threads/runs, team/workflow instances, service instances, provider endpoints, human subjects and office assignments have different lifetimes. A private port and a role title are not authority. Preserve native IDs under explicit namespaced mappings.
4. **Use explicit deployment profiles.** Preserve independent UAR/BossFang/Forge operation, optional Gate/Fabric, local embedded KnowMe and remote/home configurations. A required unsupported capability blocks placement; optional degradation is visible and never expands authority.
5. **Close real action boundaries before expanding authority.** Build on Cedar and host approval/budget machinery. Revalidate the direct, managed, embedded, queued and remote paths; authenticate instance/subject, bind the exact target and payload, compose independent boundaries restrictively, and recheck before effect. Cedar does not implement quota transactions, revocation distribution or external-effect atomicity.
6. **Extend UAR-AGENT-MD.** Preserve section-based legacy authoring and typed IR. Define five versioned document kinds with loss diagnostics and required-field rejection. Portable documents request capabilities; installed principals and representation grants stay in a private authority plane.
7. **Default to request execution or on-demand actors.** Durable state and mailbox identity are separate from residency. Measure residency and cross-host takeover needs before enabling pinned processes or transparent failover. One logical mutating turn at a time initially; cancellation/admin control stays out of that queue.
8. **Make observation a governed delivery path.** Use stable occurrence identity, per-observer inbox/cursor, an outbox at the source commit boundary and independent source/recipient checks. BossFang channel handling and observer copies have distinct routing and response rights. In-memory SSE is not a durable subscription.
9. **Preserve three data paths.** Personal authorized CRDT documents, server-authoritative business read projections, and durable offline business commands have separate stores/versions/acknowledgements. Runtime ownership, grants, budgets and external effects do not become arbitrary multi-writer CRDT objects.
10. **Start business effects with feedback intake.** Observe → classify → draft → scoped standing-policy issue creation → product/design review. Keep customer communication, roadmap promises, publication and financial actions separately authorized. Expand to marketing, design and executive support only after the governing boundaries work.
11. **Reuse the merged skill family and adapters.** Add guided role selection, reviewed skill locks and business presets through the existing creator/models/manage/handoff contracts. Keep all eight requested harnesses, including MiniMax's own CLI and DeepSeek Harness. Preserve native options with explicit passthrough/validation or unsupported diagnostics; never claim all harnesses have identical teams/plugins/marketplaces.
12. **Prefer an isolated service-console view for BossFang.** The Boss controls common connections, instances, approvals, runs, budgets and subscriptions. BossFang retains channel-specific administration. KnowMe retains personal UX and consent. Do not broaden every packaged mini-app's privileges to embed one console.

## Reuse candidates and alternatives

| Candidate | Verdict | Evidence / limit |
|---|---|---|
| Existing UAR threads, actors, graph and compiler | Adapt | R3/R5 and current source evidence. Graph scheduling and durable team semantics must be added deliberately. |
| Current Boss/UAR P1 driver, launch principal and host bridge | Adopt checkpoint | Current main contains registration and sidecar surfaces; D-UAR-P1 owns ongoing implementation and installed acceptance. |
| BossFang HTTP UAR provider bridge | Preserve | Useful native-loop mode; never relabel as delegated full-run execution. |
| Existing Cedar engine and approvals | Adapt | R5 §8 plus current startup/direct-path evidence. Governed profile semantics and policy installation need conformance. |
| Existing Fabric spine, sync and Forge APIs | Adapt checkpoint | R2; D-FRF/D-FORGE may supersede gaps. Reuse their data authority and transport contracts. |
| Agent Skills and existing team skills | Adopt | R4, merged mini/full work; lock exact revisions and validate effective runtime semantics. |
| A2A/MCP/AG-UI/CloudEvents conventions | Adapt at their boundaries | R1–R6 primary references. None grants authority, durability or live-session portability by itself. |
| New external durable workflow engine | Conditional evaluation | C10 specifies workload, recovery and embedding requirements before choosing. Prefer existing substrate if sufficient; prohibit dual schedulers. |
| Always-resident process per definition / hidden-port identity | Reject as default | R3: permanent residency adds cost without establishing durability or authority. Optional measured residency remains in scope. |
| Universal shared database or universal CRDT sync | Reject | Violates separate personal/business/runtime authorities and independent process storage. |
| Executive personas with implicit office powers | Reject | R5/R6: consent, role assignment and delegated actions require distinct trusted grants. |
